prompt: A container on Cloud Run prints `level=error msg="stock lookup failed"`. What severity does the entry get?
hint: Where does Cloud Logging read a severity from?

choices.text: ERROR, from the word after level=
choices.why: Cloud Logging does not parse text; only a JSON field named severity counts.

choices.text: DEFAULT
choices.why: Right. It is plain text with no severity field.

choices.text: INFO, the default for standard output
choices.why: The default is DEFAULT, below INFO.

choices.text: WARNING, because the line mentions a failure
choices.why: Nothing reads the words of the line.

prompt: A program writes JSON lines with the field `level` instead of `severity`. What breaks?
hint: Cloud Logging knows one of those names.

choices.text: Nothing: Cloud Logging accepts both names
choices.why: Only severity is read; level stays an ordinary payload field.

choices.text: The entries are rejected as malformed
choices.why: They are stored; that is why nobody notices.

choices.text: Every entry has no severity, so alerts on errors never match
choices.why: Right. The entries are there and invisible to every severity filter.

choices.text: The entries become textPayload
choices.why: They are still JSON, so jsonPayload; only the severity is missing.

prompt: A Python stack trace is printed over twenty lines on standard error. How does it arrive in Cloud Logging?

choices.text: As twenty separate text entries
choices.why: Right. Lesson 11 writes it inside one entry instead.

choices.text: As one entry, joined by Cloud Logging
choices.why: Cloud Logging does not join lines for a plain container log.

choices.text: As one ERROR entry, because it is standard error
choices.why: The stream does not make twenty lines one entry.

choices.text: Not at all: standard error is not collected
choices.why: Both streams are collected.

prompt: Which entries does `severity>=WARNING` select from logdemo.py's three lines?
hint: The third line has no severity.

choices.text: The WARNING line and the level=error line
choices.why: The level=error line is DEFAULT, below WARNING.

choices.text: Only the WARNING line, as jq showed
choices.why: Right. One entry, as the jq run showed.

choices.text: All three, since every line was written by the shop
choices.why: The filter is about severity, not authorship.

choices.text: None: >= cannot be used on severity
choices.why: Severities are ordered precisely so that it can.

prompt: An entry has no `httpRequest` field. Does `httpRequest.status>=200` match it?
hint: A missing field compares as nothing.

choices.text: Yes, a missing number counts as zero
choices.why: Zero would fail >=200 anyway; but missing does not match at all.

choices.text: Yes, filters ignore fields an entry lacks
choices.why: Ignoring would match everything; it does the opposite.

choices.text: No, it does not match
choices.why: Right. An entry without the field does not match, whatever the comparison.

choices.text: The query is rejected as invalid
choices.why: It is valid; it simply selects only entries with requests.

prompt: Which query is the cheapest way to find the shop's warnings in a month of logs?

choices.text: jsonPayload.message:"warn"
choices.why: A contains search on the payload reads every entry.

choices.text: textPayload=~"(?i)warning"
choices.why: A regular expression over text is the slowest of all, and misses JSON entries.

choices.text: resource.labels.service_name="shop-api" severity=WARNING
choices.why: Right. Resource and severity narrow the search quickly.

choices.text: NOT severity=DEFAULT
choices.why: That selects nearly everything, warnings and much more.

prompt: A new project's `_Default` bucket keeps entries for how long?
hint: The retention pricing starts after it.

choices.text: 400 days
choices.why: That is _Required, for audit logs.

choices.text: 30 days, then gone
choices.why: Right. Longer retention costs 0.01 USD per GiB per month.

choices.text: 90 days
choices.why: That is the shop's own bucket, chosen in Terraform.

choices.text: Until the project is deleted
choices.why: _Default has a fixed default retention, not forever.

prompt: The error sink to Pub/Sub was applied, but no messages ever arrive. The lesson's last resource was left out. Why?

choices.text: Sinks need a minute per entry to deliver
choices.why: Delivery is near real time; something refuses it.

choices.text: The sink's writer identity lacks permission to publish there
choices.why: Right. Without the IAM binding it routes nothing.

choices.text: Pub/Sub sinks accept only INFO entries
choices.why: No such restriction exists.

choices.text: The topic must be in another project
choices.why: Same-project topics are fine.

prompt: What happens to an entry dropped by an exclusion?

choices.text: It is stored but hidden from queries
choices.why: It is not stored at all.

choices.text: It is stored for 30 days, then deleted
choices.why: That is _Default's retention, for entries that are kept.

choices.text: It is never stored and never billed
choices.why: Right. Which is why the healthz noise goes there.

choices.text: It goes to the _Required bucket instead
choices.why: _Required takes only its own audit logs.

Match each JSON field to what Cloud Logging makes of it.

pairs.right: the text shown in a list of results
the trace the entry belongs to

prompt: A destination plus a filter, in the Log Router, is called a ___.
hint: Four letters; the plan created two of them.

prompt: Debug logging is left on in production and writes 1 GiB an hour. Roughly what does a 720-hour month add to the bill?

choices.text: Nothing: logs within 30 days are free
choices.why: Storing is charged once, on arrival; the 30 days are included in it.

choices.text: About 7 USD
choices.why: That would be the retention rate, not the storage rate.

choices.text: About 335 USD
choices.why: Right. 670 GiB at 0.50 USD.

choices.text: About 3,600 USD
choices.why: Ten times too much: check the price per GiB.

prompt: Put what happens to one of the shop's error lines in order.
hint: From the program to the subscriber.
items: The program prints one JSON line with severity ERROR
Cloud Run sends it to Cloud Logging
The Log Router matches the error sink's filter
The sink publishes it to shop-log-errors
trap: Matching the sink before Cloud Logging receives the line is the slip: the router only sees what has arrived.
